[USER] User requested design system component documentation for the app bars dynamic island component.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The App Bars Dynamic Island component should be used when creating a navigation bar that is fixed to the top or bottom of the screen and can expand or collapse to show more options.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The component is suitable for mobile or web applications where a dynamic navigation bar is needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The anatomy of the App Bars Dynamic Island component includes a fixed navigation bar at the top or bottom of the screen, which can have a logo, a title, and one or more options (e.g., buttons, links).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The placement of the component should be at the top or bottom of the screen, fixed in place to remain visible during scrolling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The content of the component should include a clear and concise title and clearly labeled navigation options grouped into logical categories.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The default state of the component is collapsed, showing only the most important options, and it expands when an option is tapped or clicked.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The navigation bar should remain fixed in place when the user scrolls the content.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Best practices links provided:  
1. <https://material.io/components/app-bars-top/>  
2. <https://uxdesign.cc/designing-better-navigation-bar-on-mobile-d37a501655f2>  
3. <https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2018/05/app-navigation-design-patterns/>  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional considerations for the component include responsiveness, consistent design, accessibility, customization, easy integration, and thorough testing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The interactive states of the App Bars Dynamic Island component were detailed in a table format.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Interactive states table includes:  
- Element: Navigation Bar, Option  
- States: Default, Hover, Active, Focus, Disabled  
- Properties: Background, Text color, Border  
- Color Tokens: primary, secondary, accent, focus, disabled
